plan:
I think the target is a right-hand Indian hasta where the three central fingers (index, middle, ring) are held straight and close together pointing upward, the little finger also extended but slightly separated, the thumb is flexed across the palm and its tip touches/presses near the middle phalanx/inner side of the ring finger (forming a loop across the palm). The palm faces the camera (front view). Orientation: fingers pointing upward, slight supination so the thumb is on the right of the image. Required joint placements (starting from neutral open hand):
- Index, middle, ring: MCP small flexion (~5–15°) to look natural, PIP ~0–5°, DIP ~0–5° (essentially straight)
- Little: MCP slightly abducted away from ring (+ F_abd ~10°), MCP small flexion (~0–10°), PIP/DIP near 0
- Thumb: thumb_cmc_flex positive (sweep across palm) ~30–50° to reach the ring finger, thumb_cmc_abd negative small (-10°) to bring thumb toward fingers, thumb_mcp ~20–35°, thumb_ip ~20–35°. thumb_cmc_rot slight to orient pad toward ring finger.
- Finger abductions: index F_abd slightly toward thumb side (+5–10), middle near 0, ring slight toward little (-5), little abduction more (+10)
- Whole hand: turn_hand pitch small to bring fingers slightly toward camera (~+10°) and yaw small so fingers tilt slightly right/left as in target.
I'll start by sweeping the thumb across and straightening the three central fingers, then fine-tune with looks.
